text:
erin: Quick design lane request for benchmark launch. Need compact deliverables for webinar, 3 social cards, and email hero. 48h mock, final by EOD Tue.

Deliverables checklist:
- hero diagram (latency vs unit cost) sized to read clearly at 600px width
- social cards: 1200x628, 1080x1080, 940x788
- accessible SVG for blog (WCAG color target)
- Figma page with components + export tokens
- filenames prefixed with benchmark_launch_{variant}_{size}_{date}

jordan: Copy that. I'll spin up a Figma page and set export presets. Any art direction notes?

erin: Two stylistic variants: A = data-forward (clean, chart-first), B = brand-forward (bold color, illustrated). Keep copy short.

sam: Data details: use median latency vs cost per 1k tokens for three modes: hosted, dedicated, private. Include dashed fallback curve for graceful degradation. CSV in drive: https://drive.redwood/example/benchmark-data.csv

alex: Call out SLA-preserved region for dedicated (and dedicated-burst) as a subtle shaded band with a small "SLA" badge.

jordan: For accessibility targets, aiming AA for body and AAA for headlines where feasible. Also ensure SVG export has title and desc tags.

maria: Legal: no vendor logos. Avoid absolute claims like "50% cheaper" unless backed by report. Use phrasing like "measured savings" or "up to".

nikhil: Add CTA "Request a demo" on each social card with UTM params: utm_source=social, campaign=benchmark_launch. We'll map filenames to inbound flow so ops can route leads.

jordan: Figma page created: https://www.figma.com/file/NEWFILE/benchmark-compact. Artboards: hero-600, social-1200x628, social-1080, social-940x788, blog-svg. Export presets: png@2x, svg, webp.

figma-bot: Export jobs queued for hero-600 (png, svg), social-1200x628 (png@2x), social-1080 (png@2x), social-940x788 (webp).

erin: Copy options — drop in two short lines per variant:
A (data): "Serving wins: lower latency, lower unit cost. See the numbers."
B (brand): "Inference engineered for production 12 predictable, fast, economical."

jordan: Quick design question 12 include small sparklines for day-to-day variance under the main chart or keep it minimal?

sam: Sparklines okay as micro-variance indicators, keep them subtle and below the hero chart so they don't compete for attention.

jordan: Will produce 48h mock (both A/B) and upload PDF proof. Mock page named "mock-v1" in the Figma file.

erin: When uploading finals, include final filenames in the upload note so ops can map them. I'll do a legal review after proofs are up.

maria: I'll review copy and visuals for compliance. If any claim needs a citation, we'll flag and request the test report before publish.

alex: I'll coordinate with Eng on inbound tag mapping once filenames are final. Please keep me looped.

nikhil: Prioritizing paid-social variants first for export. :thumbsup:

jordan: Mock v1 uploaded to figma (same file). Link on the page. Requesting feedback in-thread.

erin: Reviewing now, consolidated feedback incoming shortly. Thanks team!
